overview: This single-page file is a list of papers concerning a proposed underground railway in Kyoto and, more broadly, railway construction in western Japan. It records a March 30, 1931 request from the Department of Commerce for detailed information and photographs, prompted by a report from Consul Sturgeon in Tokyo, and an April 3 communication from Tokyo enclosing that request for action at the earliest practicable moment.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning an underground railway in Kyoto
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes two 1931 communications requesting information about a proposed underground railway in Kyoto or western Japan.
subfiles.summary: The first entry records that the Department of Commerce, acting on a report from Consul Sturgeon at Tokyo, requested a detailed account of an underground railway project at Kyoto, with photographs if available. The second entry records an April 3 communication from Tokyo enclosing the Commerce Department's March 30, 1931 letter and asking that full information on railway construction in western Japan be supplied as soon as practicable. The underlying correspondence is described but is not reproduced on this page.

interest: The page is useful as a compact finding aid documenting federal interest in Japanese urban-transport development during 1931. It shows how information moved from consular observation in Tokyo through the Department of Commerce and into a formal request for detailed technical reporting and photographs. Although the underlying correspondence is absent, the entries identify its dates, subject, institutional origin, and intended evidentiary material.
